items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: Joe Turner would sing and Jo Jones would have his snare drum... that was another job. We used to work there until about 7:00 the next morning... that's where I first met him, and we used to play like that.

ctx.x: So they all used to meet in the middle of the street.

Later, after -- that was the third job, because they all would leave one job around 2:00 or 3:00 or 4:00, and go to another job, you see. When I'd get off around 3:00 or 4:00 at the Cherry Blossom or any of those places, I'd go down to Piney Brown's or down there where Joe Turner was bartending. When I'd walk in, I'd have my guitar throwed across my neck.

items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] But is it true that when he was living on Long Island somewhere he had a big electric sign on his house, said King of the Blues or something? [INTERVIEWEE] No, they used his name in a club called (inaudible). The put a sign up there --

ctx.x: No, we just did the last few things he had. The rest of it he had done. But I had to show him, so that show was really going over. Back in New York, they said, man, they got 5,000 or 6,000 tonight and all blues, don't want to hear not -- (inaudible) same key, same tempo, (inaudible) the girl, right after her and then Larry with the band come on, (inaudible).
But is it true that when he was living
on Long Island somewhere he had a big electric sign on his house, said King of the Blues or something?
